triage.note: GREEN BEFORE AND AFTER, deliberately: this is the far-side guard for every boundary the other four cases move. Period end 2006-12-31 is sixteen days past the 33-8732A compliance date, so Items 10 and 13 must carry the MODERN captions here while nike-2006 (2006-05-31) carries the legacy ones -- a correction that overshoots by pushing the boundary any later than 2006-12-15, or that drops the modern alias while adding the legacy one, dies on this case and lives on nike-2006. It is authored in the same pass as the red cases and asserted at the same time, because a boundary correction with only the near side pinned is a correction that can be satisfied by deleting the far side. No check here fails before the fix; that is the point, and it is the same role the SigmaRenoPro golden plays for the 2016 taxonomy (sgrp-2019-shallow provenance: 'expected GREEN with no new code ... worth as much as a red one only because the assertions are strong enough to have failed').

provenance: AUTHORED FROM THE COMMITTED FIXTURE, no new fixture: Bank of America FY2006 10-K, period ending 2006-12-31 (full public-source provenance in evals/fixtures/README.md; see also bac-2006-shallow.json). AUTHORITY: Release 33-8732A for Items 10 and 13 (fiscal years ending on or after 2006-12-15); Release Nos. 33-8048 / 34-45189 for Item 12's suffix (fiscal years ending on or after 2002-03-15); Release 33-8400 for Item 15's loss of the 'and Reports on Form 8-K' clause (effective 2004-08-23, keyed here at the period end 2004-05-23 the table already uses for ADDED['9B'], the same release). CORPUS NOTE, and the reason the labels here are canonical rather than copied: this filer's own headings LAG the rules it is subject to for two of the five items -- 'Item 5. Market for Registrant's Common Equity and Related Stock Holder Matters' (no issuer-purchases clause, and 'Stock Holder' as two words) -- while writing the current caption for Items 10, 12, 13 and 15. Both facts are visible in the same document, which is a compact demonstration that filer wording cannot be the ground truth for an era label. The item 5 check pins the current ALIAS_FROM['5'] value (2005-12-01) as behaviour, NOT as a claim that the date is right: the diff that produced this case found Item 5's modern caption is more likely bound to Release 33-8335 ('Purchases of Certain Equity Securities by the Issuer and Others', periods ending on or after 2004-03-15), and no committed fixture has a period end between 2004-03-15 and 2005-12-01 to tell the two dates apart. That gap is recorded as open debt in tasks/TODO.md. CORRECTED (PR #17 round 1): this check does NOT catch that move. Asserted at period end 2006-12-31 it bounds ALIAS_FROM['5'] from ABOVE only -- setting the constant to 2004-03-15 left this case, the whole fast suite (51/51), the invariant suite (13/13) AND the module self-check green on the pre-repair tree; as of the round-1 assert the self-check is what stops it (AssertionError at segment.py, exit 1), while this case and both suites stay green exactly as stated. What catches an earlier move is the two-sided assert added to segment.py::_demo in the same round; this check's real job is the upper bound, i.e. it goes red at date(2007,1,1) and later. WATCHED (green) in the same run as the four red cases -- see the commit that adds this file. NOT yet dual-passed by extraction-auditor: pending, per case-authoring step 8.
